A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VideoNIAH and VNBench. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables, equations, and task examples, support reliable comparison. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original VNBench and VNBench-Long evaluations, task analyses, and experiments varying model size, frame sampling, visual tokens, and temporal prompts.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds action-clip evaluations, comparisons with real-world benchmarks, construction-robustness tests, and answer-consistency analyses.

M1.justification: The synthetic construction procedure, CLIP filtering, and core circular scoring rule remain unchanged. Dynamic video-clip needles were already allowed in v2 Section 3.1; VNBench-Act evaluates that possibility. Appendix G expands documentation of the retained training model without establishing an architecture or objective change.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on VideoMME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench in Appendix B.2. VNBench-Act adds retrieval, ordering, and counting of action-bearing clips from Something-Something V2, extending evaluation beyond static-image and subtitle needles. Something-Something V2 already appeared in the training mixture; its new evaluation role is the coverage change.

E2.justification: The evaluated model families and size variants remain present in the corresponding VNBench comparisons. Added experiments use models already evaluated in v2. Appendix J adds a 25% chance reference but does not document an additional evaluated comparison method.

E3.justification: Figure 8 changes from binary extraction outcomes to accuracy averaged over 32 distinct samples. New protocols compare 1350 versus 2700 samples, replace needle content at matched positions, and evaluate six frame-count configurations across real-world benchmarks. Appendix J introduces consistency and conditional-accuracy metrics. The main four-pass circular evaluation remains unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds analyses testing agreement with real-world benchmarks, sensitivity to needle content and dataset size, and answer-option consistency across nine subtasks. It also revises the position-depth analysis using multiple samples. Existing model-configuration ablations and the one-to-four-pass circular-evaluation analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report correlation coefficients and one-to-four option-shuffled evaluations. v3 adds no seed information, independent-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. Averaging 32 distinct test samples changes evaluation design; the new consistency scores are evaluation metrics rather than uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial cross-benchmark, action, robustness, and consistency results. For example, Table 6 reports GPT-4o action retrieval, ordering, and counting scores of 85.6, 11.3, and 10.0. Main Table 2 remains unchanged, but the detailed 30–60-second LLaVA-OneVision-7B overall score changes from 69.8 to 60.0, ending its reported tie with 72B. Several counting cells are also corrected between v2 Table 6 and v3 Table 11.

T1.justification: Appendix J introduces definitions of answer consistency and conditional accuracy, with the reasoning that circularly correct predictions form a subset of consistent predictions. This mathematical treatment is absent from v2. Appendix G also formalizes visual-token construction and the training loss, without introducing a new theorem or demonstrated method change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about scalable synthetic construction, skill-specific evaluation, VNBench's three task families, and insights for video-model development. The new experiments support these claims without redefining their central scope.

C2.justification: Appendix J materially qualifies low-score comparisons: option-order sensitivity can affect circular accuracy, and Counting-E2 differences should not be interpreted as meaningful capability advantages. New discussion interprets real-benchmark correlations, construction robustness, and action-ordering failures. The existing Section 7 limitation about synthetic data complementing real-world benchmarks remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix G newly documents the visual-token and answer-loss computations and training for one epoch on 16 NVIDIA A100 GPUs. Added analyses disclose sampling and replacement-needle details. Conversely, v3 removes the abstract's code/data availability statement and project link without replacing them elsewhere; the PDFs do not establish that the resources themselves became unavailable.

R1.justification: v3 adds ChatBridge and a brief discussion of integrating external modalities, a Something-Something citation, and Wang et al. and Wei et al. on multiple-choice evaluation and selection biases. The broader positioning against existing video benchmarks and synthetic language-model evaluations remains stable.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include local wording and typo corrections, expanded training explanations, an acknowledgment section, conference headers, and appendix subdivisions accommodating the new analyses. There is no extensive rewrite of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 5 is redrawn with separately identified OneVision size variants, and Figure 8 replaces binary maps with annotated continuous-accuracy heatmaps and a color scale. v3 adds eight tables, a cross-benchmark correlation figure, and animal-needle illustrations. It also relocates existing plots and corrects illustrative options and table labels.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the benchmark's validation: Appendix B.2 tests its relationship to real-world performance, F.2–F.3 examine construction sensitivity, and Appendix J explains why some low-score rankings are misleading. These address important evidential and interpretive gaps in v2. The validation remains limited to the tested configurations, while removal of the project link and Table 8's conflicting Ordering-I1/I2 labels weaken reproducibility. Nevertheless, the targeted evidence and more careful interpretation provide a substantial net improvement.
